# Checklist: api
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 002-cms-conteudo | Date: 2026-09-05 -->

Requirement **quality** checks for the API surface. Implementation verification lives in
[`../tasks.md`](../tasks.md).

**Most of this surface is generated, which is exactly why it needs checking.** Payload derives
REST and GraphQL from the collection configs, so nobody writes an endpoint and nobody reviews
one — the contract is the field definitions and the access functions. Two endpoints *are*
hand-written: the presign request and the download counter.

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK063 | The spec states that no HTTP surface is hand-authored except the two named, so a reader knows the generated surface is the contract. **OPEN — the two named endpoints are not the ones that shipped.** There is no presign route (`presignUpload` has no production caller), and `scopedListEndpoint` is a hand-authored surface registered on every scoped collection, which this preamble does not account for | [contract] | FR-021 | [ ] |
| CHK064 | Because the surface is generated, the requirement is explicit that **access control is the contract** — a boolean where a constraint belongs opens every generated endpoint at once | [contract] | FR-006, FR-024 | [x] |
| CHK065 | The presign request's inputs are defined: which collection, which field group, and the declared size. **OPEN — no presign endpoint exists.** D1 removed the presigned path; `lib/uploads/presign.ts` is dormant | [contract] | FR-012, FR-016 | [ ] |
| CHK066 | The presign response is bounded — what it returns and how long the URL is valid. **OPEN — no presign endpoint exists**, so it returns nothing and no URL validity window applies | [contract] | FR-012 | [ ] |
| CHK067 | The presign endpoint is stated to enforce the cap **as policy on the signed URL**, not as a value it trusts the client to respect. **OPEN — no signed URL is issued.** The cap is enforced inside Payload own create operation instead; see CHK034 for why that is a supersession rather than a substitution | [validation] | FR-012, SC-007 | [ ] |
| CHK068 | The presign endpoint's own authorization is stated — who may request one, since an unauthenticated presign is a free write to the bucket. **OPEN — no presign endpoint exists** to authorize. The equivalent question on the native path — who may create a media document — is answered by `scopedAccess()` on the three media collections, but no requirement states it | [validation] | FR-012 | [ ] |
| CHK069 | The download endpoint is defined as **open, no account**, and the requirement says so rather than leaving it to be inferred | [contract] | FR-015 | [x] |
| CHK070 | The download endpoint's cross-organization behaviour is specified as a **404**, not a 403 — a 403 confirms the document exists | [errors] | SC-010 | [x] |
| CHK071 | The counter write is specified as passing through the tenancy choke point, with the organization resolved from the host | [validation] | FR-016 | [x] |
| CHK072 | Rejection reasons are required to name **what was wrong** — the offending value and the expected shape — not "invalid input" | [errors] | SC-006, SC-007 | [x] |
| CHK073 | The 404-versus-403 rule is consistent across the generated surface too: another organization's document is absent, never forbidden | [errors] | SC-002, SC-010 | [x] |
| CHK074 | Draft and in-review documents are stated as absent from public responses, not merely filtered from listings | [contract] | FR-010 | [x] |
| CHK075 | The published-only rule is stated to apply to **GraphQL and REST alike**, since both are generated from the same config. Delivered differently and more strongly: neither generated API serves an anonymous reader (`scopedAccess` opens `if (!user) return false`, and the plugin refuses a no-membership session outright), so the published-only rule is not a per-protocol filter at all — `getPublicScopedPayload` is the single public surface | [consistency] | FR-010, SC-002 | [x] |
| CHK076 | Relationship population is named as a surface: a public read that populates a relation must not populate an unpublished or foreign row. **OPEN — and this is a live gap, not a wording one.** `getPublicScopedPayload` forwards the caller `depth` while running `overrideAccess: true`, and the published-only filter is applied to the queried collection only. `evento` relates to `projeto` and to `aula`, both publishable, so a public read at depth 1 populates a row that may be in `rascunho`. No test covers population on the public path | [validation] | FR-010, SC-002 | [ ] |
| CHK077 | Field labels are PT-BR while field **names** are English, and the requirement says which side each falls on — the API contract is the names. **OPEN — the field names are PT-BR.** `titulo`, `imagemCapa`, `curtidas`, `aprovacaoRegistrada`, and the slugs with them. That may well be right for a product whose page specs are PT-BR, but the API contract is the names, Principle 4 says code is English, and no requirement states which way this falls | [contract] | FR-001 | [ ] |
| CHK078 | The `status` enum values are fixed and enumerated, since they travel in API responses and feature 003 will filter on them | [contract] | FR-008 | [x] |
| CHK079 | Derived fields (`curtidas`, `downloads`, `formatos`, `totalModelos`) are marked as read-only in the contract, so a client cannot write them directly. **OPEN — the counters carry `admin.readOnly` and nothing else.** That is admin-UI cosmetics, the exact lesson `aprovacaoRegistrada` records two fields away, where a real `access.update` guard is present. A client can PATCH `curtidas` or `downloads` directly | [validation] | FR-020 | [ ] |
| CHK080 | Adding a collection is stated as additive; renaming or removing a field is called out as a **breaking change** for feature 003. **OPEN — stated nowhere.** Neither the spec, the plan, the data model nor the CHANGELOG says that adding a collection is additive while renaming or removing a field breaks feature 003 | [versioning] | FR-001 | [ ] |
| CHK081 | Lexical JSON is named as the stored shape of rich text, so feature 003 plans a renderer rather than discovering the format | [contract] | FR-001 | [x] |
| CHK082 | The storage swap is stated to change no API surface — env only, `forcePathStyle` true→false | [versioning] | FR-019, SC-011 | [x] |
